Your tools start at the FLEET root (/home/vgpnk/Projects/shokunin), so a relative lane path lands in the wrong repo.

Read first: /home/vgpnk/Projects/shokunin/mado-shokunin/.ufo/waves/round-31/registration.md (the frozen registration: C1 row-fidelity gate PRED-C1-r31, C2 resolved-citation counter v2 PRED-C2-r31-v2, C3 hardened index gate PRED-C3-r31, kill rules, routed queue). It is FROZEN: attack it in your report, never edit it, and never edit .ufo/waves/round-31/c2/count.py, quality/check-index-rows.py or quality/check-index.py — they are the measured artifacts. Base=274f7355366d38d6e78f641ad62472e68df4686a; data commit=f621e3c004858e01334f4de4ccffe8693a137da6.

Report only at .ufo/waves/round-31/w1/reports/<YourName>.md inside the lane repo. Lane bytes are read-only for every seat; run counters, never edit them. Evidence = committed bytes at named revisions (`git show REV:path`) plus exact command transcripts.

items.name: ExecC1Rerun
items.prompt:
RUNNER (no writes beyond your report).

Re-run the C1 row-fidelity gate at both revisions from /home/vgpnk/Projects/shokunin/mado-shokunin: `python3 -I quality/check-index-rows.py --rev 274f7355366d38d6e78f641ad62472e68df4686a --repo .` (expect `rows=43 errors=1` with `row-cells: knowledge/animation-table-r26.md at line 52 carries 2 cells`, exit 1) and `--rev f621e3c004858e01334f4de4ccffe8693a137da6` (expect `rows=43 errors=0`, exit 0). Then `--selftest` (expect `10/10 assertions passed`) and `--root .` on the worktree. Record every line + exit code. Attack: try to make a row pass the gate while sitting outside the coverage-map table, or with a third cell that never quotes its note — a control that produces errors=0 on a falsified row is a kill-rule K1 hit; report it.

items.name: ExecC2Rerun
items.prompt:
RUNNER (no writes beyond your report).

Re-run `python3 -I .ufo/waves/round-31/c2/count.py` at 274f7355366d38d6e78f641ad62472e68df4686a (expect `UNRESOLVED criterion 35` … `TARGET_MISSED`, exit 1) and at f621e3c004858e01334f4de4ccffe8693a137da6 (expect `resolved_active=41/41` `TARGET_MET`, exit 0). Then run all four negative fixtures: `python3 -I .ufo/waves/round-31/c2/count.py --active-min 2 --quality .ufo/waves/round-31/c2/negative/<d>/corpus/QUALITY.md --lessons-root .ufo/waves/round-31/c2/negative/<d>` for d in n1-empty n2-wrongfile n3-section n4-collapse. Expected: n1 UNRESOLVED empty file; n2 TARGET_MET (existence is the rubric; flag as a residual cheat); n3 UNRESOLVED wrong section; n4 FLOOR_VIOLATION. Record each verdict + exit. Attack: construct a fifth fixture that drains the denominator or cites a nonexistent section differently — e.g. `Supersedes criteria 1-53` on an umbrella line, or a spell-form `lesson round99 M1` against an absent file. If any drains-to-MET or resolves-to-MET, the kill rule K2 fires; report.

items.name: ExecC3Rerun
items.prompt:
RUNNER (no writes beyond your report).

Re-run `python3 -I quality/check-index.py --selftest` (expect `12/12 assertions passed`), `--rev 274f7355366d38d6e78f641ad62472e68df4686a` and `--rev f621e3c004858e01334f4de4ccffe8693a137da6` (both `indexed=43/43`), `--root .`, and the adversarial calls: `--rev=--output=/tmp/x` (expect SETUP_ERROR exit 2, no /tmp/x* created), `--root <dir-with-symlinked-corpus>` (expect REFUSED exit 1), `--root . --repo /nonexistent` (expect SETUP_ERROR exit 2). Build the symlink fixture under /tmp yourself. Record each exit + stderr. Attack: any invocation that either silently writes outside /tmp (SentScope F5 residual) or certifies a tree it should have refused is a K3 hit; report.

Record.

items.name: ScribeCriteria
items.prompt:
WRITER of no lane files; your report only.

Audit new rows 53 and 54 of corpus/QUALITY.md at f621e3c004858e01334f4de4ccffe8693a137da6: (a) does row 53 restate criterion 48's rule verbatim (byte-compare the rule text), and does its citation `lessons/round-23.md#final-c1-disposition-withdrawn-to-base-bytes-honest-stop M23-7` resolve to a real heading + real table row in corpus/lessons/round-23.md; (b) does row 54's claim about the round-30 rubric match `.ufo/waves/round-30/registration.md` and the r30 counter's actual behavior; (c) does the corrected criterion-35 citation now point at the section that actually contains M23-7. items.name: ScribeRecords

items.name: CritPredicates
items.prompt:
FALSIFIER. Attack PRED-C1-r31 / PRED-C2-r31-v2 / PRED-C3-r31 as the r30 wave attacked its predecessors: every control is a committed revision in a scratch clone, fixtures under /tmp only, lane bytes read-only.

(a) C1: `check-index-rows.py` measures README *row fidelity* — table region, >=3 cells, resolvable paths, Holds overlap. Can a row with three non-empty cells and resolvable cites still lie (e.g. Holds paraphrases a different note; sources cell cites real S-ids that describe nothing)? Build the control. (b) C2: `count.py` v2 resolves file#anchor and spell-form citations — can a criterion resolve its citation while citing a lesson whose content contradicts the rule (resolution is syntactic; relevance is out of scope — is that a loophole the kill rule misses)? Build the control. (c) C3: the gate now refuses option-shaped revs and symlink ancestors — find another adversarial surface: `--repo` pointing at a different repo whose tree coincidentally matches; a rev that's a tag pointing at an unsigned blob; `--root` on a bind-mount-looking path. Report any TARGET_MET on a control that skips the claimed work.

items.name: CritKillRules
items.prompt: FALSIFIER of the round-31 kill rules K1/K2/K3 (see registration). For each, build the cheapest committed state that satisfies the predicate while failing its intent: K1 (a row that errors=0 but is not a faithful index row), K2 (a state that reaches TARGET_MET without every active criterion being grounded — e.g. via supersession edge cases, or a criterion with zero grounding cites but trivially-resolving `outside` corroboration), K3 (a mutation that changes gate behavior while all 12 selftest assertions still pass). Controls under /tmp; lane read-only. Report which kill rules fail to rule out their cheapest shortcut.

items.name: RevC1Rows
items.prompt: REVIEWER (report only). Read `quality/check-index-rows.py` at f621e3c004858e01334f4de4ccffe8693a137da6 line by line. Check: the `table_region` boundaries (does a row after `## Quality bar` get rejected?), the cell-count rule on a row whose third cell is `| |`, the Holds-overlap threshold (5 shared words — can a generic sentence like 'How X works and the tool that checks it' reach 5 words against a different note?), glob-vs-literal classification on paths like `.ufo/evidence/round-12/drift-*.txt` (which WARN rather than ERROR — is that the right call when the r12 evidence is ephemeral?), and the `outside`-only criterion loophole (a criterion whose only grounding is `outside R13-V1` — does it resolve, and should it). Report concrete findings with line citations.

items.name: RevC2Resolution
items.prompt: REVIEWER (report only). Read `.ufo/waves/round-31/c2/count.py` at f621e3c004858e01334f4de4ccffe8693a137da6 line by line. Check: GitHub slugification parity for the `### Final C1 disposition: withdrawn to base bytes (honest stop)` heading (spaces, colon, parens, hyphens — does the counter's slug function produce exactly what GitHub anchors generate?); the `outside` corroboration rule (a criterion with ONLY `outside` cites — resolved or not, and what does the docstring claim); the ACTIVE_MIN=30 floor (does a fixture with `--active-min 2` still honor the other kill conditions); the ITEM_RE `item 1` rule (criteria 11-14 use `item 1` — do they resolve, or is item 1 silently absent everywhere and WARN-less); the seeded-criterion non-superseding path. Report.

items.name: RevC3Gate
items.prompt: REVIEWER (report only). Read `quality/check-index.py` at f621e3c004858e01334f4de4ccffe8693a137da6. Check: `rev-parse --verify --end-of-options` on refs like `master^{commit}` vs raw `master`; `%(objecttype)` filter for symlinks-at-rev (blob-only — verify a symlinked `.md` under corpus/knowledge in a committed tree IS a `blob` type and counted — parity with the fence, which counts it); `os.path.commonpath` ancestor checks (does a root that is itself a symlink pass or refuse); the `--root + --repo` SETUP_ERROR (is the error text accurate). Also re-run the 12-assertion selftest independently. Report.

items.name: MutGates
items.prompt:
MUTATE-RUN-REVERT probe (report only; lane restored byte-identical after each run).

Mutate `quality/check-index-rows.py` and `quality/check-index.py` in a scratch clone under /tmp (never in the lane): (a) for the rows gate — remove the `table_region` check, lower the overlap threshold to 1, make glob-nomatch an ERROR; run --selftest + a seeded defect each; does each mutant change at least one assertion outcome (killed) or pass silently (survivor — report). (b) for check-index — remove `--end-of-options`, drop the ancestor-containment check, make `--repo`+`--root` allowed; each must be killed by one of the 12 assertions or reported as a survivor. Table: mutant | expected detector | killed/survived.

items.name: SentScope
items.prompt:
SECURITY review (report only; lane read-only; /tmp fixtures only).

Re-probe the C3 gate's adversarial surface after the r31 hardening: (a) a `--rev` value that IS a valid ref yet weird (`refs/heads/../x`, unicode branch name, a ref whose tree entry for corpus is a submodule/gitlink — mode 160000 — does `ls-tree` show it and does the gate count it as a note?); (b) `--root` where `corpus` is a hardlink-heavy tree or a mount point; (c) `--root` where `corpus/knowledge` contains a FIFO (non-regular — expect REFUSED); (d) `--root` on a path containing `..` components. Each must produce REFUSED/SETUP_ERROR, never a silent pass or a write outside /tmp. Also verify no code path in check-index-rows.py / count.py can write outside /tmp (no open(...,'w'), no subprocess without capture). Report.

Report.

items.name: RevengerRowGap
items.prompt:
READ-ONLY (report only).

Reconstruct how the r26 README row lost its Sources cell: `git log --follow -p corpus/README.md` around the row's lifetime; name the commit that dropped the `| source:` cell (or prove it was never there), and check whether the r30 fence would ever have caught it (it wouldn't — that's the C1 blind spot).
